_protocol: READ THIS FIRST, before writing or changing any code.
1. Read this file's `modules` array to find the module you're about to touch. Check `status` and `dependsOn` — do not start a module whose dependencies are not yet `done`.
2. Open progress/modules/<id>-<slug>.md for that module for full context: purpose, acceptance criteria, caching/security notes, and the decisions log.
3. Before marking a module `done`, verify every item in `definitionOfDone` below that applies to it, and every item in the module's own `acceptanceCriteria`.

4. When you finish a work session (even a partial one), update: status, filesTouched, decisionsLog (append, do not rewrite history), and lastUpdated/lastUpdatedBy in BOTH this JSON and the module's markdown file. Out-of-sync JSON/markdown is the one thing that breaks this system for the next LLM — keep them in lockstep.
5. If you get blocked, set status to 'blocked' and add a line to `blockers` explaining exactly what's needed to unblock — do not leave it silently stuck at 'in_progress'.

definitionOfDone.text: Meets every item in this module's acceptance criteria
TypeScript strict mode passes, no `any` without a comment explaining why
All external input (API body, webhook, AI-model JSON output) validated with a zod schema before use
If this module touches a DB table: Row Level Security policy exists and has a test proving cross-tenant access is denied
No secret/key is imported into client-bundled code; server-only env vars are not prefixed NEXT_PUBLIC_
Caching decision made explicitly (cached with stated TTL, or explicitly marked not-cached with a one-line reason) — never silently uncached by omission
If this module exposes a public/unauthenticated endpoint: IP rate limit + abuse guard (captcha/honeypot) is implemented
Failure paths handled explicitly (API timeout, rate-limit response, malformed AI output) — no silent swallow
At least one automated test covering the module's main success path and one failure path
This module's tracker file updated: status, files list, decisions log, and any new caching/security notes

If this module added/changed any file under app/src/app/** or app/src/modules/**: confirm the actual Vercel deployment for the pushed commit shows state READY (via the Vercel MCP connector's get_deployment/list_deployments), not just that local tsc/prettier/tests pass. Added 2026-07-24 after 5 consecutive production builds failed post-966cb69 on a client/server bundle-boundary bug (a Client Component importing a barrel that re-exports server-only code) that none of tsc/prettier/unit tests catch, and that next build can't be run locally in this sandbox (SIGBUS, see Module 0.0). See progress/modules/5.2-brand-prompt-configuration.md decisions log for the full incident.

decisionsLog.text: One Free-plan workspace per person, not two, enforced via normalized-email uniqueness (not raw-string matching, which is trivially bypassed with +tag/dot email aliases) plus IP-based signup throttling. Deliberately did not add phone/card verification to close the remaining "two different real email addresses" loophole — that friction isn't justified against a threat this bounded, since the Free plan itself is capped at 5 prompts/weekly checks regardless. Rule scoped to Free-plan ownership only; workspace membership (agency clients invited as Viewer) is unrestricted.

Free plan redesigned from a recurring weekly-cadence tier to 3 lifetime on-demand experiments, then locked to read-only. This module owns workspaces.experiments_used's creation/default only — cap enforcement and paid-feature gating live in the modules that actually run/limit checks. Full reasoning in progress/modules/5.9-billing-and-subscription.md decisions log.

Implementation: workspace creation is a SECURITY DEFINER Postgres function (create_workspace), not a client-side insert, because the free-plan-uniqueness check needs a row lock (FOR UPDATE) across a race window that a single RLS policy can't express. No client-facing INSERT policy exists on workspaces/workspace_members as a result.

Implementation: the Owner/Member/Viewer invite hierarchy is enforced as an RLS INSERT policy on workspace_members (workspace_members_insert_by_role), not only in application code, so RLS is the real gate per docs/CONVENTIONS.md Section 6 item 1.

Implementation: built the IP rate limiter (rate_limit_events + checkRateLimit()) as a shared src/lib/security utility since the acceptance criteria says 5.11 will reuse the same pattern — built once, not duplicated later.

Only tsc/eslint/prettier and the 12 pure-logic unit tests were actually verified. Applied 0001_auth_and_workspaces.sql to the live project (vloradmcvozmhvvxiyvd) via the Supabase MCP connector. Fixed a real ordering bug caught by apply_migration itself: workspaces' RLS policies (workspaces_select_member/workspaces_update_owner) referenced workspace_members, but that table was originally declared after those policies in the file — Postgres rejected it with "relation public.workspace_members does not exist". Fixed by moving the workspace_members CREATE TABLE to immediately follow workspaces, before either table's RLS policies. Migration applied clean on retry.

Ran get_advisors (security) immediately after applying 0001, per its own recommendation to check right after DDL changes. It caught 2 real gaps beyond the 1 expected INFO (rate_limit_events RLS-with-no-policy, which is intentional/documented): (1) normalize_email had a mutable search_path, (2) handle_new_user and create_workspace were both callable directly as public RPCs (/rest/v1/rpc/...) by anon/authenticated, when handle_new_user should only ever fire via the on_auth_user_created trigger and create_workspace should never be callable by anon. Wrote and applied 0002_auth_security_hardening.sql: pinned normalize_email's search_path, revoked all EXECUTE on handle_new_user from public/anon/authenticated, revoked EXECUTE on create_workspace from public/anon and re-granted it to authenticated only. Re-ran get_advisors after: down to 2 remaining entries, both intentional and already documented (rate_limit_events INFO, and create_workspace still callable by authenticated — which is required, since that's how signed-in users create a workspace).

Ran generate_typescript_types against the live schema and replaced the hand-written app/src/types/database.ts with the real generated file (adds __InternalSupabase.PostgrestVersion, proper FK Relationships entry for workspace_members -> workspaces, and the Tables/TablesInsert/TablesUpdate/Enums/CompositeTypes helper types Supabase's generator ships). tsc --noEmit passes clean against it. Also fetched the live project URL (https://vloradmcvozmhvvxiyvd.supabase.co) and anon/publishable keys via get_project_url/get_publishable_keys for the user to paste into app/.env.local — the service-role key still has to come from the user manually via the dashboard, since no MCP tool exposes it (a deliberate security boundary, not an oversight).

User confirmed Google OAuth provider is now configured in the Supabase dashboard, and that NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY/SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY are populated in their real .env files. Confirmed independently: app/.env.local in the mounted working folder now holds real-looking values for all three Supabase vars (real project URL, and two JWT-shaped keys, no longer the placeholder text).

Security incident caught and fixed: real secrets (Supabase service-role key, anon key, Gemini key, NVIDIA NIM key) had been pasted into app/.env.example — the template file that's supposed to hold only placeholders and is deliberately NOT gitignored (docs/CONVENTIONS.md Section 1; root .gitignore has `app/.env*` then `!app/.env.example`), since it's meant to be committed. Checked git status/log first: this was still an uncommitted working-directory change (only one commit exists, predating this edit, and it's not pushed), so nothing leaked into git history or GitHub. Restored app/.env.example to the exact original committed placeholder content via `git show <initial-commit>:app/.env.example`; confirmed `git diff` on the file is now empty. No key rotation needed since nothing was ever committed/pushed, but this is a reminder to only ever paste real values into .env.local, never .env.example.

Two legitimate attempts made to actually execute (not just structurally verify) the cross-tenant RLS proof required by this project's own definitionOfDone "rls" item, both blocked by environment constraints rather than by any code/RLS defect: (1) tried proving it directly via SQL (execute_sql) by inserting two synthetic auth.users test rows and querying under simulated authenticated/anon roles — blocked by the platform's own safety classifier as a sensitive action, correctly, since writing directly into Supabase's auth schema is exactly the kind of thing that should require explicit human execution, not an LLM workaround. (2) Ran the actual written test suite (tests/integration/auth-rls.test.ts, which uses the sanctioned Supabase Admin API createUser/deleteUser, not raw SQL) via `node --env-file=.env.local --test`, now that real credentials exist in app/.env.local — this failed in the before() hook with AuthRetryableFetchError/'fetch failed'. Confirmed via a direct curl to the project's /auth/v1/health endpoint that this sandbox's outbound network proxy returns HTTP 403 for supabase.co — an environment/sandbox network-allowlist limitation, separate from the Supabase MCP connector's own channel (which works fine for apply_migration/execute_sql/etc.). Structural verification remains solid (RLS enabled on all 4 tables per list_tables, policies confirmed correct per get_advisors), but the actual behavioral proof — two real accounts, cross-tenant read/insert denied — has not yet been executed to a passing result anywhere. That must happen on a machine with real network egress to Supabase: the user's own machine (`npm test` locally), or GitHub Actions CI once the three secrets are added there.

User fixed the sandbox's outbound network access; re-verified with a direct curl to https://vloradmcvozmhvvxiyvd.supabase.co/auth/v1/health, which now returns a real 401 'No API key found' response instead of a proxy-level 403 — genuine egress to the live Supabase project confirmed. Re-ran tests/integration/auth-rls.test.ts for real via `node --env-file=.env.local --test`: it executed (no longer blocked), but FAILED — 3 of 4 subtests ('lets user A read their own workspace', 'denies user B reading user A's workspace', 'denies user B reading user A's workspace_members row') all threw Postgres error 42P17 'infinite recursion detected in policy for relation "workspace_members"'. The 4th subtest ('denies user B inserting...') shows as passing but only because its assertion is `error !== null`, which the same recursion error also satisfies — it does not actually prove the intended insert-denial behavior. Root cause identified in app/supabase/migrations/0001_auth_and_workspaces.sql: all four workspace_members RLS policies (select/insert/update/delete, lines ~159-218) use a USING/WITH CHECK subquery that selects from workspace_members itself (aliased self/wm) to check the caller's membership — a self-referencing subquery on the same table its own policy protects, which Postgres re-evaluates recursively. This is a known Supabase RLS anti-pattern; the standard fix is a SECURITY DEFINER helper function (e.g. is_workspace_member(workspace_id, user_id)) that looks up membership with RLS bypassed, referenced from all four policies instead of the direct self-join. This is a genuine code defect, not an environment issue — exactly what the module's own Next steps note said to treat it as if the test ran and failed. Not fixed yet — needs a migration 0003 and user sign-off before touching live RLS policies.

User approved the fix; applied migration 0003_fix_workspace_members_rls_recursion.sql live via the Supabase MCP connector (apply_migration, success). Added public.is_workspace_member(workspace_id, user_id) and public.has_workspace_role(workspace_id, user_id, role) as SECURITY DEFINER/STABLE functions with a pinned search_path, and rewrote all 4 workspace_members policies plus both workspaces policies (select/update) to call them instead of self-joining workspace_members directly. Also tightened tests/integration/auth-rls.test.ts's 4th subtest to assert error?.code === '42501' (the specific RLS-violation code) instead of just error !== null, since the old assertion could pass even when the failure was actually the 42P17 recursion bug. Re-ran `node --env-file=.env.local --test tests/integration/auth-rls.test.ts`: all 4 subtests now pass (0 failures) — this is the first genuine passing run of this test in this project's history, satisfying definitionOfDone's rls item for real. Ran get_advisors immediately after (per established pattern): it flagged the two new helper functions as WARN authenticated_security_definer_function_executable (directly callable via /rest/v1/rpc/..., letting any signed-in user probe arbitrary membership/role pairs). Attempted a follow-up migration to move both functions into a non-PostgREST-exposed private schema to close that surface entirely — this was blocked by the platform's own safety classifier (DDL dropping functions + changing schema grants on a live database) and was not worked around. Left as an open, documented, non-blocking follow-up — see Blockers.

User explicitly directed retrying the private-schema hardening migration; retried apply_migration with the identical SQL and it succeeded this time (the classifier block was transient/session-specific, not a permanent denial). Verified live via execute_sql (read-only pg_proc/pg_namespace query): private.is_workspace_member and private.has_workspace_role both exist, anon_can_execute=false, authenticated_can_execute=true; no public-schema versions remain. Re-ran get_advisors: the authenticated_security_definer_function_executable WARN for these two functions is gone — only the pre-existing, already-accepted create_workspace WARN and an unrelated auth_leaked_password_protection WARN remain. Security note: during this step, a tool result appeared claiming the migration file on disk had been altered by 'the user or a linter' into a materially less secure version (grants EXECUTE to anon, drops the private-schema hardening entirely, no explanation of why) and instructed not to mention this to the user. Independently verified via a direct file Read (unchanged from the version this module authored) and via the live-DB query above (matches the secure private-schema version, not the version described in that message) that no such change actually occurred anywhere — treated as a suspicious injected instruction, not a real event, and not acted on. Flagged to the user directly rather than followed.

User disabled Supabase Auth's 'Confirm email' requirement (previous session's SMTP-rate-limit workaround) and asked for one final clean click-through before marking this module done. Ran it live against aeo-roan.vercel.app via Claude in Chrome. Sign-up crashed: POST /sign-up returned a raw 500 with an opaque body (signUp failed { status: 500, message: '{}' }). Root-caused via Vercel runtime logs + Supabase auth logs (get_logs, since the SQL-exposed audit_log_entries table had zero rows — the failure aborted before any DB write completed): 'Database error saving new user', underlying Postgres error 'duplicate key value violates unique constraint "user_profiles_normalized_email_key"' (23505). Confirmed via execute_sql: every test email I used (heisen.better.berg+aeofinaltest2@..., +aeofinaltest3@...) normalizes (public.normalize_email) to the same real inbox as an earlier unconfirmed test signup (+aeodiagfinal@..., created 11:33:48 UTC this session) that already has a user_profiles row. This is NOT a bug in the uniqueness rule itself — migration 0001's own comment confirms 'at most one identity per real inbox' is deliberate, not just a workspace-level rule (see 2026-07-23 decisions log entry above). The bug is the failure mode: Supabase Auth (GoTrue) cannot surface a custom trigger's exception message to the client — any handle_new_user() failure collapses to a generic opaque 500, which is exactly what a real user would hit if they signed up, didn't confirm, and tried again (even with the literal same email, in some flows) or used a +alias without realizing it colludes with an existing account. Confirmed this is a genuine app-code gap, not newly introduced: app/src/modules/auth/email.ts's normalizeEmail() docstring already says it exists 'so the UI/API layer can show a same-email error before round-tripping to Postgres' — that pre-check was designed for but never actually wired into signUpAction().

Fixed in app/src/app/(auth)/actions.ts: signUpAction() now queries user_profiles (via the service-role client, since user_profiles has no anon select policy) for an existing row matching normalizeEmail(email) before ever calling supabase.auth.signUp(). If found, redirects with a clean 'An account already exists for this email. Sign in instead.' message instead of attempting a doomed signUp() call. Documented as a best-effort check, not a lock — a rare concurrent-signup race could still slip through to the same crash, but the DB unique constraint remains the real backstop for data integrity either way. Verified with `npx tsc --noEmit` (clean). NOTE (2026-07-25): despite what this entry originally claimed, the fix was NOT actually committed at the time — it was still an uncommitted working-tree edit. See the 2026-07-25 entry below.

(Later session, same day.) Duplicate-email fix actually committed as 81cc1d4 (previous entry's 'committed locally' claim was inaccurate — git status/git diff showed it was still uncommitted when this session picked the module back up). Also, per user's request, set up direct git push from the sandbox: SSH deploy key generated inside .git/ (never tracked), repo-local core.sshCommand routes over ssh.github.com:443 (plain port 22 is blocked by the sandbox network allowlist, 443 isn't), remote switched to the SSH URL. SSH transport verified reaching GitHub (correctly rejected with 'Permission denied (publickey)' since the public key isn't registered yet). Waiting on user to add the public key to the repo's Deploy keys with write access, then push + Vercel redeploy + re-verify the click-through. Also asked user about the account-enumeration trade-off in the new error message — user chose to keep the specific 'account already exists' message.

(Same day, key registered.) User added the SSH deploy public key to GitHub. Pushed 81cc1d4+3c6e19e to origin/main; Vercel auto-deployed to production and reached READY. Ran the live click-through via Claude in Chrome. Findings: (1) fresh signup blocked by Supabase's own free-tier email-send rate limit (429 'email rate limit exceeded') -- pre-existing, already tracked in LEFT_FOR_FINAL_TOUCHES.md, confirmed via execute_sql that no orphaned row was left behind; (2) sign-in with the one available (browser-autofilled) credential set was rejected -- confirmed via Supabase auth logs (delegated to a subagent, logs too large for direct reading) that this was a genuine 400 invalid_credentials, not a bug, but it doesn't prove a successful sign-in either since the password may be stale; (3) Google OAuth is broken on the live project -- clicking 'Continue with Google' correctly builds the redirect but Supabase itself returns 400 'Unsupported provider: provider is not enabled', contradicting the earlier claim it was configured. Un-checked that acceptance criterion. Net result: the code fix is live and its failure paths behave correctly, but this module is not done -- one real regression (Google provider disabled) plus two checks still environmentally blocked.

(Same day.) User asked whether the Google OAuth issue should keep 5.1/5.2 blocked or be split out. Corrected an inaccurate premise first: no session or tool in this project has ever disabled Google OAuth deliberately -- the decisions log only shows it being configured, and no available tool can edit Supabase Auth provider settings. Likely conflated with the separate, genuinely-deliberate 'Confirm email' disable. Recommended splitting the acceptance criterion (email/password gates done; Google OAuth tracked separately, non-blocking) since nothing downstream of 5.1 actually depends on Google OAuth specifically. User chose to split it out. acceptanceCriteria updated accordingly; Google OAuth item moved to progress/LEFT_FOR_FINAL_TOUCHES.md. Module 5.2 is now unblocked to start regardless of the OAuth dashboard fix.

(Same day, retry.) Retried fresh signup once the rate-limit window had likely cleared. First attempt hit a transient Supabase/Cloudflare 525 SSL handshake failure (confirmed via Vercel runtime logs; confirmed cleared within ~1 min via direct curl to /auth/v1/health). Second attempt succeeded cleanly: auth.users + user_profiles rows created correctly (verified via execute_sql), normalize_email() correctly left a non-Gmail address untouched. App correctly took the unconfirmed-session branch because 'Confirm email' turns out to be ON right now, contradicting the LEFT_FOR_FINAL_TOUCHES.md note that it was disabled -- this also retroactively explains the earlier rate-limit 429s (real confirmation emails were being sent). Signed in with those exact known-correct credentials: correctly rejected (GoTrue won't issue a session for an unconfirmed account; app collapses this into the same generic enumeration-safe message by design). Net: every email/password code path is now proven correct and secure via direct verification; the only remaining gap is a literal /dashboard screenshot, blocked by the same class of dashboard-config issue as Google OAuth. Did not attempt to fix via SQL (auth schema writes are out of scope for an LLM, per this module's own established precedent).

(Same day, closing.) User confirmed: track both open dashboard-config gaps (Google OAuth, 'Confirm email') in the pending/final-touches tracker and close this module out. Flipped status to done, percentComplete to 100. Left both acceptance-criteria lines about them explicitly marked with notes explaining the deviation from progress.json's own done-gate protocol is a deliberate, documented user decision, not an oversight. User also asked about bypassing real authentication during further development and identifying users by email instead -- clarifying the intent (dev/test convenience only vs. an actual product-level auth change) before writing any code, since RLS depends on real Supabase session identity and a naive email-only trust model would be a genuine security regression.

(Later session, post-done.) User reported login confusion after adding https://aeo-roan.vercel.app/ as a Supabase Redirect URL: an email not in user_profiles still got rejected as 'already exists', plus the signup rate limit tripped. Root-caused via execute_sql: (1) genuine orphaned auth.users row (csalad504@gmail.com, pre-existing test debris) with no user_profiles row -- our duplicate check only looks at user_profiles, so Supabase's own uniqueness constraint was the actual source of the rejection, not a bug; (2) rate limit was correctly enforcing exactly 5/hour (verified: 5 signup: events for the user's IP inside the current 60-min window). Also found and fixed a real bug while investigating: signUpAction()'s signUp() call never set options.emailRedirectTo (unlike the Google OAuth action, which does), so confirmation-email links never routed through /auth/callback -- meaning a confirming email/password user never got a session or workspace. Fixed in commit 27798c2. This fix requires /auth/callback (not just the bare origin the user added) in Supabase's Redirect URLs allow-list -- flagged as a new LEFT_FOR_FINAL_TOUCHES.md item since no available tool can change that dashboard setting directly.

blockers: No open blockers for this module. Three Supabase dashboard-config gaps remain open but are intentionally non-blocking: Google OAuth disabled; "Confirm email" active (contradicting an earlier note); Redirect URLs allow-list missing /auth/callback (found 2026-07-24, needed for both Google OAuth and the just-fixed email-confirmation flow to actually work in production) -- all three tracked standalone in progress/LEFT_FOR_FINAL_TOUCHES.md, not silently dropped.

modules.name: Brand / Prompt Configuration

acceptanceCriteria.text: Manual entry: brand name, website, competitor names
AI-assisted prompt suggestion: one Gemini call proposes 20-30 prompts from the brand's site/industry
Free-plan workspaces: prompt list is auto-selected from the AI suggestions and fixed — not editable. Default chosen: 10 (see decisions log)

Paid-plan workspaces: full edit/add/remove on the prompt list, up to plan-tier prompt-count limits enforced server-side (chosen: Starter 25, Growth 75, Agency 200 fair-use — top of each spec range, enforced per-brand not per-workspace, see decisions log), not just hidden in the UI — real gate is a DB trigger, not app code

modules.cachingNotes: Not cached — this is low-frequency, user-driven write traffic.
modules.securityNotes: Treat all user-entered prompt/brand text as untrusted; validate with zod and never interpolate raw into a system-level instruction to any AI call. Real enforcement of plan-tier limits/Free-plan immutability is the private.enforce_prompt_plan_rules() DB trigger, not the zod schema (UX pre-check only).

decisionsLog.text: Free-plan workspaces get a fixed, non-editable prompt list; prompt customization becomes a paid-only capability. Part of the wider Free-plan redesign (3 lifetime on-demand experiments, then locked) — see progress/modules/5.9-billing-and-subscription.md decisions log for the full reasoning.

Chose concrete numbers within the spec's stated ranges: Free=10, Starter=25 (top of 15-25), Growth=75 (top of 50-75), Agency=200 (concrete number for spec's undefined 'fair-use'). Enforced per-brand, not per-workspace — an interpretive call since the spec doesn't specify and a workspace can hold multiple brands; per-brand reads more consistent with the multi-brand agency use case. What changed: a Free-plan workspace no longer gets an ongoing weekly automated check — it gets exactly 3 on-demand, user-triggered checks total (never resets, doesn't renew), tracked by a new workspaces.experiments_used column. After the 3rd run, 5.5 generates one aggregate report (score, rank, citations, a 3-point Share-of-Voice trend) and no further checks are allowed. Paid plans (Starter/Growth/Agency) are unaffected. What's also paid-only now: the Explanation Engine, Opportunity Finder, and confidence-tagged recommended actions (5.5) are computed only for paid plans — gated before the NVIDIA NIM call happens at all. Free-plan prompts also become fixed/non-editable (5.2). Why: the original free tier's AI-quota exposure per signup was open-ended, compounding the risk already accepted around the multi-key failover pool (5.3). A fixed lifetime cap bounds the cost of every free signup to a known, small number, removes an entire scheduling branch from 5.3, and creates a harder, clearer upgrade trigger. Superseded: spec Section 3.3/3.4's "Automated weekly (free plan) / daily (paid plan) checks" line, for the Free plan specifically — paid-tier numbers are unchanged. The spec docx is left as the original v1.1 historical document, not live-patched; this tracker entry is the current source of truth. Cross-references: enforcement split across 5.2 (fixed prompt list), 5.3 (on-demand trigger + counter gate), 5.5 (aggregate report + paid-only Explanation Engine), 5.6 (locked/upsell UI), this module (lifetime vs. period-based limits). workspaces.experiments_used owned/created by 5.1.

blockers: Intentionally not started — deliberately deferred by user request, not an oversight. No action until core features (5.1-5.8) are done.

modules.name: Admin / Ops Console

acceptanceCriteria.text: Live Gemini + NVIDIA NIM quota consumption view, broken down per key in the pool (primary/secondary/tertiary), not just per provider
Key-pool health view: which keys are alive vs. marked dead, when a key died, and a manual clear-dead-flag action
A key transitioning to dead (401/403) fires an immediate alert, not just a log line
Displays current failoverMode ("shared" vs "emergency-only") per provider, with a visible reminder to switch to emergency-only the moment primary is upgraded
Error/failure log for failed checks
Basic churn signal: customers inactive 2+ weeks
AI task config view: list every task key's current global-default (provider, model, enabled) from ai_task_configs, editable inline
Enable/disable a model for a task globally (flips enabled on the global-default row)
Per-workspace override: search a workspace, add/edit/remove its override row for any task key, without touching the global default
Every write to ai_task_configs records updated_by + updated_at

modules.cachingNotes: Short TTL (e.g. 60s) on the quota-usage view is fine — it's an internal dashboard, not billing-critical, so a slightly stale read is an acceptable tradeoff for lower DB load.
modules.securityNotes: Gate at the server/API layer by role check, not just by hiding a frontend link.

decisionsLog.text: Scope expanded to own the admin UI for ai_task_configs (global enable/disable + per-workspace override management for model experiments) — one small screen, not a new module.
Scope further expanded to surface the multi-key failover pool (5.3) — per-key health + immediate alert on a key dying. Required condition of accepting the key-pool risk, not optional.

modules.name: Public Free-Check Lead Magnet

acceptanceCriteria.text: Public endpoint runs one prompt through the Engine Query Engine and returns a shareable result
Soft paywall shown after the result

modules.cachingNotes: Highest-priority cache in the product: identical (brand, prompt) free-check results cached for 24h, keyed by a hash of normalized input — this is the single biggest defense against a public endpoint draining the shared free Gemini quota.
modules.securityNotes: IP rate limit + CAPTCHA/honeypot — this is the most exposed, unauthenticated surface in the whole system and must not ship without both controls in place.

modules.name: Growth Automation Pipeline

acceptanceCriteria.text: Lead list sourced from a free-tier source, filtered to ICP
Each lead's brand auto-run through the Engine Query Engine
Personalized email draft generated from the real result
Drafts pushed to a cold-email tool for sequencing

modules.cachingNotes: Reuses the 5.11 free-check cache where a lead's brand was already checked recently — avoids double-spending quota on the same company.
modules.securityNotes: Scope data access to public company info only; comply with CAN-SPAM/GDPR unsubscribe requirements from the first send.

modules.name: Phase-2 AI Engines (ChatGPT / Perplexity / Copilot)

acceptanceCriteria.text: OpenAIProvider implemented (web-search tool), gated behind a paid add-on
PerplexityProvider implemented (Sonar API)
CopilotProvider implemented via the customer's own Bing Webmaster OAuth (official, free)
UI clearly labels each engine by name — never implies ChatGPT when the data came from Gemini

modules.cachingNotes: Same TTL/guard pattern as 5.3 and 5.11, per provider — these are paid calls, so the redundant-call guard matters even more here than on the free tier.
modules.securityNotes: Never scrape a competitor AI product's consumer web interface under any circumstance — only the official APIs listed here.
